input_text: Web API on AKS with 3 Standard_D4s_v5 nodes, Azure SQL Database General Purpose 4 vCore provisioned, Redis Premium P1 cache, all in West Europe. About 2,000 users, busy in business hours, quiet at night. Data must stay in the EU.

components.details: Web API hosted on AKS; SKU tier not stated, assumed Standard
3 worker nodes of size Standard_D4s_v5 running the Web API; busy during business hours, quiet at night

constraints.notes: Around 2,000 users, busy in business hours and quiet at night. Data must stay in the EU.

options.details: Consumption plan, Linux, web API 1 vCPU 2 GiB per replica, min 2 replicas always on, scale out on HTTP load during business hours, scale down at night, EU region
options.rationale: Replaces the AKS control plane fee and all three D4s_v5 worker nodes with per-second billed replicas that scale with the business-hours load, so night-time cost is minimal.
tradeoffs: Less Kubernetes-level control (no custom operators or DaemonSets)
Needs the API to be containerised and stateless
Cold-start if min replicas set to 0

meters.why: Active vCPU seconds: 2 replicas x 1 vCPU, assume ~8 busy hours x 22 days ~ 176h; 2 x 176h x 3600s ~ 1.27M, plus scale-out replicas -> ~2.16M s (assumption)
Idle vCPU seconds: min 2 replicas x 1 vCPU idle for remaining ~554h x 3600 ~ 3.9M s (assumption)
Active memory: 2 GiB x same active seconds as vCPU (2.16M) = 4.32M GiB-s
Idle memory: 2 GiB x 3.9M idle seconds = 7.8M GiB-s
Assume ~5M HTTP requests a month for 2,000 users (assumption)

options.details: Linux, 2 instances, zone-redundant not required, autoscale to 1 instance at night, containerised Web API
options.rationale: Fully managed PaaS with no cluster fee or node management and autoscale matches the day/night pattern, costing far less than AKS plus 3 D4s_v5 nodes.
tradeoffs: Less flexible than Kubernetes for multi-service architectures
Scale-out is slower than container replicas
Fixed per-instance pricing while running
options.effort_reason: Managed PaaS with autoscale; containerising the API and moving off AKS takes effort

meters.product: Azure App Service Premium v3 Plan - Linux
meters.why: P1v3 Linux plan, 2 instances during business hours; modelled as always-on (night scale-down to 1 not credited: conservative)

options.details: Free tier control plane, no uptime SLA, keep a small system node pool plus autoscaled user pool of Standard_D2as_v5 nodes
options.rationale: Keeps Kubernetes but drops the paid control-plane fee and lets the autoscaler use cheaper AMD nodes.
tradeoffs: No financially backed uptime SLA
Limited to smaller clusters (about 1000 nodes cap)
Still requires cluster operations effort

meters.why: Free tier control plane: only the free-tier infrastructure cost meter applies, billed all month for 1 cluster

options.details: Linux, AKS node pool with cluster autoscaler, 2 nodes minimum scaling to 3 in business hours, AMD EPYC
options.rationale: The same 4 vCPU and 16 GiB as D4s_v5 at a lower hourly price on AMD, and autoscaling removes the idle third node at night.
tradeoffs: AMD vs Intel CPU, slight performance variance
Node pool must be recreated to change the VM size
Autoscaler scale-up takes a few minutes
options.effort_reason: AKS on VMs with autoscaler still needs cluster and node maintenance; new to team

meters.why: Regular Linux D4as_v5, 3 nodes priced always on (matches today's 3 nodes; autoscale to 2 at night not credited)

options.details: Linux, AKS node pool with cluster autoscaler, 3 to 6 nodes, 2 vCPU 8 GiB AMD
options.rationale: Smaller AMD nodes track the load more finely and cost less per node, so the pool can shrink further when quiet.
tradeoffs: More nodes means higher per-node system overhead
More pod scheduling fragmentation
Needs resource requests tuned

meters.why: Regular Linux D2as_v5, minimum 3 nodes always on (autoscale up to 6 not assumed)

options.details: General Purpose serverless, min 0.5 vCore max 4 vCore, auto-pause after 1 hour of inactivity, ~30% active, EU region
options.rationale: Compute is billed per second only while active, so the quiet nights cost almost nothing and daytime load still scales up to 4 vCore.
tradeoffs: Cold-start delay of up to a minute after an auto-pause
Storage is billed even when paused
Heavy sustained load can cost more than provisioned

options.rationale: A smaller flexible-server compute is generally cheaper than 4 provisioned SQL vCores for around 2,000 users and has no per-core licence component.

Different tooling and feature set

options.rationale: The cheapest option if the cache holds only small, easily rebuilt data like sessions or lookup values.

Data lost on node restarts or patching

rejections.reason: The alternative sets min replicas to 2, so scale-to-zero cold start does not apply; however this entry is not flagged for that rule (no violation).
The Free AKS tier has no financially backed uptime SLA for the API server, which is unsuitable for a production Web API serving 2,000 business users.
Serverless with auto-pause makes the first connection after an idle period wait up to about a minute to resume, which hurts a user-facing API at the start of the business day.
Redis Basic C0 is a single node with no replication and no SLA, meant only for development and testing, not a production cache.

Today's P1 cache is Premium, and Standard lacks persistence, clustering and VNet injection, so replacing it is only valid if none of these are used; the details do not show they are needed, so this is not a violation.

plans.name: Cheapest
plans.summary: Moves the Web API to App Service (which removes the separate worker VMs), switches the database to PostgreSQL Flexible Server and shrinks Redis to Standard C1, all in West Europe so data stays in the EU. This is the lowest-cost combination but involves the most change.
tradeoffs: Database move from SQL Server to PostgreSQL requires schema and query migration and app changes
App Service is less flexible than Kubernetes if you add more services later
Redis drops to 1 GB with no persistence, so check cache size and usage first
Largest migration and testing effort of the three plans
plans.note: Moving everything to northeurope would save only $26.15/mo more (4.9%), not enough to justify a region migration, so this plan stays in westeurope.

Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server General Purpose Ddsv5 Series Compute / vCore

plans.name: Balanced
plans.summary: Keeps AKS and SQL Database but uses an autoscaling AMD node pool, a 2 vCore SQL database and Redis Standard C1, all in Sweden Central (inside the EU). This captures much of the saving without changing the application platform or database engine.
tradeoffs: Moving region from West Europe means a data migration and a short cutover
SQL 2 vCore has less peak headroom, so check CPU utilisation before downsizing
Redis C1 has only 1 GB and no persistence
AMD nodes and autoscaler scale-up delay may slightly affect peak responsiveness
plans.note: Moving everything to swedencentral saves $52.56/mo (5.2%) more than staying in westeurope. Plan for the data migration and check latency for your users.

SQL Database Single/Elastic Pool General Purpose - Compute Gen5 / vCore

plans.name: Safest
plans.summary: Everything stays in West Europe on the same services. Only the AKS node pool is switched to a cheaper autoscaling AMD size and the SQL database is trimmed to 2 vCore, while Redis Premium stays untouched.
tradeoffs: Smaller saving than the other plans because Redis P1 and AKS stay as they are
SQL 2 vCore has less headroom and should be checked against real CPU usage first
Changing the node pool VM size requires recreating the pool
No data migration or region move needed

SQL Database Single/Elastic Pool General Purpose - Compute Gen5 / vCore

suggestions: Switch AKS to the Free control-plane tier (or keep Standard only if you need the uptime SLA) and buy 1-year or 3-year Azure Reserved Instances / Savings Plan for the three D4s_v5 nodes (~30-40% savings).
Enable cluster autoscaler and right-size: scale nodes down to 1-2 (or use a smaller SKU like D2s_v5) at night and off-hours; consider Spot node pool for non-critical workloads.
Replace Redis Premium P1 with Standard C1 (or Basic for dev/test) unless you need persistence, clustering, or VNet injection; or reserve capacity if Premium is required.
Use SQL Database serverless (auto-pause/scale) or reserved capacity with Azure Hybrid Benefit for the 4 vCore General Purpose DB; right-size vCores based on actual utilization.
